title: The Lighter Brief
overview: A pretty upbeat mix today: Jamaica is about to release its 1,000th rescued rock iguana, Fall Out Boy are heading out on a big 2027 stadium tour, and the FDA approved a brand-new kind of stroke-prevention pill. On the civic side, Charlotte locked in a long-term airport deal, and a lame-duck congressman is pushing for a House vote to impeach the Defense Secretary.

stories.headline: Charlotte signs a long-term airport deal with American Airlines
stories.summary: Charlotte City Council voted 8-2 on Monday to approve a new lease that keeps American Airlines' hub at Charlotte Douglas for at least another decade. The deal opens the door to about $2.1 billion in airport upgrades. Supporters called the airport the engine of the local economy. Critics raised concerns about worker pay for airline contractors and about fares.
key_facts: Lease runs 10.5 years, with an option for a five-year extension
About $2.1 billion in projects, including an expanded Concourse C, a passenger tunnel and a renovated international pavilion
American's gates will grow from 93 to 109
Contracted workers said they earn $12.50 an hour; state law bars the city from setting their minimum wage
stories.why: If you fly out of Charlotte, expect more construction, more gates and likely more direct flights. A consumer group warns that fares could go up.

stories.headline: Jamaica's comeback iguana hits a big milestone: 1,000 back in the wild
stories.summary: On Saturday, the 1,000th Jamaican rock iguana raised at Hope Zoo will be released into the Hellshire Hills. The species was declared extinct in 1948, then rediscovered in 1990. Thirty-plus years of head-starting baby iguanas and trapping predators have helped the wild population grow. Conservationists are celebrating but say the job isn't done yet.
key_facts: Hope Zoo raises roughly 250–300 young iguanas at a time until they're big enough to fend for themselves
More than 1,500 predators, such as mongooses and feral cats, have been removed from the iguanas' core habitat
More than 280 live predator traps are monitored
Jamaica has protected just over 25% of its land and aims to pass 30% within about a year and a half
stories.why: A species once written off as gone is now breeding on its own in the wild again, a real conservation success story.

stories.headline: Outgoing GOP congressman forces a vote on impeaching Hegseth
stories.summary: Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) introduced eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The articles mainly concern military action in Iran without congressional authorization. The move starts a 48-hour clock for the House to act. The effort is expected to fail while Republicans hold the majority, but Massie says he hopes it pushes President Trump to name a replacement before Democrats take control of Congress in January.
key_facts: Massie lost his May primary and leaves Congress in January
Three articles cite the War Powers Resolution over Iran
Hegseth called the effort a 'sham'; Trump said he stands by him
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said he's a 'hard yes'
stories.why: This is an early sign of how the Iran conflict could shape the agenda when control of Congress changes hands in January.

stories.headline: Workers treated after white powder found at NC recycling plant
stories.summary: Workers at Prime Recycling in Caldwell County, N.C. reported coughing, burning eyes and trouble breathing after a white powder on packages went airborne. Officials said those taken to the hospital are in stable condition. State investigators and hazmat teams are working to identify the substance.
key_facts: 22 people were assessed at the scene
Reports of how many went to the hospital range from 11 to 14
The facility was evacuated as a precaution
disputed: The substance has not been identified yet
stories.why: The good news so far is that everyone affected is reported stable, with answers still to come.

stories.headline: Merl Grove teachers protest their principal
stories.summary: About 40 teachers at Merl Grove High School in St Andrew, Jamaica, held a silent protest calling for Principal Dr Marjorie Fullerton to resign. They allege an authoritarian, retaliatory leadership style. Fullerton was reinstated this year after a court ruled in her favour over her 2022 dismissal. She could not be reached for comment.
key_facts: The protest began around 10:30 a.m. Monday and disrupted classes
Board chairman David Hall is asking the Education Ministry to step in urgently
Fullerton returned to the school in April
disputed: The teachers' complaints are allegations; Fullerton has not responded publicly
stories.why: The board is asking the Education Ministry to step in quickly so the dispute doesn't affect students.

links.title: Merl Grove teachers revolt over principal’s leadership style

stories.headline: Jamaica's school board chairs told to stay in their lane
stories.summary: JACSI, Jamaica's association of secondary-school board chairmen, says some chairs are drifting from governance into day-to-day school management. The group wants to train boards to focus on policy and oversight and leave daily operations to principals.
key_facts: JACSI President Courtney Wynter was re-elected unopposed to a second term
50 boards were represented at the annual general meeting
Wynter says the Education Regulations of 1980 give boards wide powers
stories.why: Clearer roles between boards and principals could mean fewer standoffs like the one at Merl Grove.

links.title: JACSI moves to rein in school chairmen overstepping roles

stories.headline: Jamaica's tourism boss wants the boom to lift everyone
stories.summary: Dr Carey Wallace of Jamaica's Tourism Enhancement Fund says tourism growth should build wealth across the whole country, not just for those in the industry. He pointed to the 'Tourism 3.0' push to get more Jamaicans supplying what tourists buy. He also said new hotel rooms coming online should help the sector bounce back from Hurricane Melissa.
key_facts: The government targets $10 billion in earnings and 10 million visitors by 2036
Jamaica rose from 82nd to 78th on the World Economic Forum's tourism index
Rondel Village resort in Negril marked its 40th anniversary
stories.why: It's an optimistic plan to spread tourism money more widely as Jamaica rebuilds.

stories.headline: Cardi B and Jamaican festival organisers trade lawsuit threats
stories.summary: BZR WKND organisers say Cardi B was paid in full but skipped both the October show and the December makeup date, and they plan to sue. Cardi B says she got only a deposit and threatened to countersue. Ticket buyers are being refunded.
key_facts: Organisers say they paid US$2.5 million
Cardi B says she received a US$1 million deposit
The festival was scheduled for October 16–18
disputed: The payment amount is disputed: organisers say US$2.5M was paid in full, Cardi B says only a US$1M deposit
No lawsuit has been confirmed as filed; both sides are only threatening legal action
Refunds for fans are confirmed by the organiser's CEO
stories.why: If you bought a ticket, the organiser's CEO says everyone will get their money back.

links.title: Cardi B threatens legal action against BZR WKND organisers
